thread:
maya: Heads-up — after the 1767bb merge I'm seeing a perf regression on our g4-large canary. Latency p50 jumped ~35% and we got a compile storm in the logs. @ravi can you take a look?

ravi: Saw the alert. Quick glance at the runtime logs shows repeated kernel compilations for the same op id. Suspect the autotune mapping table is picking a different kernel variant and invalidating cached kernels.

alex: Reproduced locally with the replay harness. Repro command: `./tools/replay_load --model=redwood-7b --seq=1024 --batch=1 --tokens=20000`

jamie: CI also failed the perf gate on the nightly job: https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/4982 — perf diff shows compile time spike and increased tail latency.

ravi: Dumped the autotune entry for the conv kernel: `autotune::lookup(op=conv2d, hw=ampere, sz=256) -> variant=A1 (was B3 before)` — A1 triggers a different JIT path.

maya: Any clue why lookup changed? Did the autotune cache TTL or keying change in the last PR?

alex: The merge touched kernel-key hashing in compile manager (1767bb). I can bisect.

ravi: Bisect note: reverted 1767bb locally and latency goes back to baseline, compile storm disappears. So 1767bb is a likely culprit.

ci-bot: perf-gate failed — regression +18% p99 on nightlies (job id: 4982).

jamie: We should block the rollout until we either revert or patch keying. Can we do a minimal fix to restore previous key semantics?

ravi: Minimal fix idea: preserve old kernel key prefix (model_arch + seq_len_bucket) while we evaluate new hashing. Patch branch ready: `fix/kernel-key-preserve-1772`

maya: Nice. Can you open a revert PR as backup and a forward-fix PR? If revert is simpler, do that first. Add testcase in compile_manager_test to prevent regression.

alex: Opened forward-fix PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/6721 — preserves old prefix and emits debug metric `kernel_key_mismatch` when lookup changes.

ravi: Also added a small regression test that runs the replay harness for 2k tokens and asserts no repeated compiles:```
# test snippet
out = run_replay("redwood-7b", seq=1024, batch=1)
assert out.compile_count["conv2d"] <= 1
```

jamie: Can we add a short-term mitigator in the runtime to avoid invalidating KV cache on kernel-key change? Losing KV cache is hitting latency badly.

ravi: I've added guard: if kernel_key_changed && compile_time < 10ms then skip invalidation. Push in PR now.

maya: Great. Please run the nightly perf job on the branch. Also flag the canary to block rollout until we have a green perf gate.

ci-bot: Triggered perf job for branch fix/kernel-key-preserve-1772 (build 4989).

sre-bot: Canary routing paused for release v0.42.3 per slack request from @maya.

alex: Early perf numbers from build 4989 look promising — p50 back to baseline, compile_count down to 1 per op in the replay. Still running full nightlies.

ravi: Note for postmortem: autotune table mutation without a migration path caused variant flip + kernel-key skew -> repeated JIT + KV cache invalidations. We should add a compatibility check in autotune writes.

maya: Agreed. Once CI finishes, we'll either merge the fix or revert 1767bb. Thanks all for quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

jamie: Filing a follow-up ticket to add continuous test in perf CI that runs the replay harness on canary nodes every deploy to catch this earlier (ticket RED-1129).

alex: FYI I captured logs and flamegraphs here: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/4989/flamegraph.svg — shows hotspot in compile_manager::emit_jit

ravi: I'll follow up with a short postmortem and include the autotune key spec.

maya: Marking resolved for now once PR lands and perf gate passes. Keep the thread updated.
